intro.h2: Kitchen Remodeling in Waukesha, Planned Before It Is Priced
paragraphs: Most homeowners looking at kitchen remodeling in Waukesha want a straight answer on cost. GMH Construction puts its numbers on the site: a standard kitchen remodel runs about $75,000 to $100,000 and up, and a premium remodel about $105,000 to $160,000 and up. Your own price follows a design phase, not a guess.

That design phase is the core of how GMH works. A Design Retainer covers the time with their designers, so the scope, selections and budget are settled before construction. Most projects then move to a fixed-price contract: unless you change the scope or selections, the quoted price does not go up.

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Custom cabinets, countertops, islands, layered lighting, flooring and storage. Standard remodels may include minor wall changes and moved fixtures over 12 to 16+ weeks. Premium remodels use higher-end materials and can move walls or windows, over 14 to 18+ weeks.

image.alt: Hartland, WI kitchen remodel with dark granite island top, wood cabinets, glass pendant lights and an open sightline to the dining area

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Main baths, primary suites and three-quarter baths with custom cabinetry, showers and tubs, lighting and flooring. Pricing assumes a full gut and remodel, and an interior designer works with you through the whole project. Most baths take 8 to 12 weeks.

image.alt: Three-quarter bathroom remodel with glass walk-in shower, gray subway tile accent, white vanity and granite top

items.name: Basements and Lower Levels
items.blurb: Full lower-level build-outs with three-quarter bathrooms, wet and dry bars, family rooms and home theaters. Projects include utilities, framing, insulation and flooring. A Hartland lower level features a bar with seating beside a brick fireplace.

image.alt: Hartland, WI basement remodel with wet bar, quartz peninsula, glass-front cabinets and brick fireplace

items.name: Additions and Sunrooms
items.blurb: Room additions, three-season and four-season sunrooms, and whole-house remodels that open up older floor plans. One Delafield family wrote that GMH removed walls and staircases that other bidders called impossible, and rebuilt their entire first floor.

image.alt: Brookfield, WI home addition with vaulted ceiling, dark timber trusses, wide windows and wood floor dining area

items.name: Signature Series
items.blurb: A budget-friendly, semi-custom option for kitchens, baths and basements with little to no structural change. You choose from a curated set of popular materials. Published ranges: kitchens $65,000 to $80,000, main baths $35,000 to $48,000, owner baths $50,000 to $65,000.

image.alt: Waukesha, WI bathroom remodel with wood double vanity, white quartz top, black mirrors and black hexagon floor tile

items.title: Owners on your job
items.text: Greg or Dane meets you, plans the project and writes your bid, then stays present at your home through construction. Both are reachable by cell phone.

items.title: Fixed pricing
items.text: Most projects run on a fixed-price contract. Labor and materials are included, and the price holds unless you change the scope or selections.

items.title: A Design Center to see it first
items.text: Explore cabinetry, countertops, fixtures and finishes in person with GMH designers, who also work with the production team so the design can actually be built.

items.title: Clean, connected job sites
items.text: Crews clean up daily, and a client wrote that GMH runs a large HEPA air filter to keep dust out of the house. JobTread keeps schedule, finances and documents in one app.

about.text: GMH Construction, Inc. has been remodeling homes in Southeast Wisconsin for over 30 years and is a licensed general contractor in the state. It is owner-run: Greg Perkins and his co-owner Dane meet homeowners, plan projects, write bids and stay on site through construction. Designers Robin and Audrey lead the design phase, and Julie keeps schedules moving behind the scenes. The firm is an active NARI member and holds an A+ rating with the BBB. Many clients come back; one testimonial describes a kitchen, foyer and family room job as a second remodel with GMH.

image.alt: GMH Construction carpenters installing kitchen cabinets in a Waukesha County home

process.h2: How a GMH Project Is Planned and Priced

steps.title: Consultation at your home
steps.text: An owner meets you at home to walk the space, set the scope and explain how pre-construction works.

steps.title: Design Retainer
steps.text: About 2 to 3 weeks later, GMH presents a Design Retainer with the scope, a budget range and estimated designer time.

steps.title: Design and selections
steps.text: Designers guide your choices at the Design Center and finish with a set budget and a detailed scope of work.

steps.title: Construction contract
steps.text: Sign the contract, usually fixed-price, and set your start date. Crews generally work from 7:00 to 4:00.

service_area.h2: Lake Country and Waukesha County Service Area
service_area.text: GMH works from its office on Westmound Drive and remodels homes throughout Waukesha County and Southeast Wisconsin. Its most common service areas are Waukesha, Pewaukee, Brookfield, Elm Grove, Hartland, New Berlin, Delafield, Menomonee Falls, Merton, Sussex, Lake Country and Oconomowoc. Testimonials also come from homeowners in Bayside and Whitefish Bay, so call if your town is a little farther out.

items.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Waukesha County?
items.a: GMH lists a standard kitchen remodel at about $75,000 to $100,000 and up, taking 12 to 16+ weeks, and a premium remodel at $105,000 to $160,000 and up, taking 14 to 18+ weeks. The semi-custom Signature Series kitchen runs about $65,000 to $80,000. Final pricing depends on room size and features.

items.q: What does a bathroom remodel cost?
items.a: With standard finishes, a typical 45-square-foot main bath starts around $45,000 and a primary bath around $70,000. Premium finishes start around $60,000 and $90,000. Prices assume a full gut and include labor, materials, flooring, countertops and fixtures. Most baths take 8 to 12 weeks.

After the first meeting at your home, GMH follows up in about 2 to 3 weeks with a Design Retainer. It outlines the scope of work, a project budget range and the estimated time with their designers. That design work produces an accurate budget and a detailed construction contract, usually at a fixed price.

One of the owners, Greg or Dane, meets you to plan the project and write the bid. Designers Robin or Audrey and their team handle design, specifications and pricing. Once work starts, Greg and Dane are present at your home throughout, and both are always reachable by cell phone.

items.q: What hours do crews work, and how will I stay informed?
items.a: Crews generally start at 7:00 and finish at 4:00, though GMH works with each family on start times. Communication runs through JobTread, which reaches several team members at once and shows your schedule, finances and documents. For emergencies, the team can always be reached by phone.

final_cta.text: Book a free consultation at your home and see what your project would take.
